review_candidates.title: Principal Research Scientist and Director of Health Research
review_candidates.description: Job Summary The Principal Research Scientist and Director of Health Research leads the health research and development portfolio at Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA), providing oversight to the Applied Research & Methods (ARM) team’s health projects and leading the de velopment of health-focused programs across the organization. The position will sit within the ARM team, which designs and leads technical research for IPA's global program portfolio, with a focus on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-experimental impact evaluations, and survey methodology. The person in this role will set the technical direction for ARM's health-focused research and assure the quality of that work.The current portfolio includes large-scale household surveys, biomarker collection, and research that draws on routinely collected health data. The role carries responsibility for hiring, supervising, and developing a team of research scientists and research support staff. It also includes serving as senior researcher on selected surveys and studies, depending on the pace of building the tea m. Much of the work in the initial two years will be focused on providing intellectual leadership on specific studies in Sub-Saharan Africa, although the role is global in nature. The person in this role will also work closely with IPA’s Business Development and Sector Programs teams to provide leadership and strategic guidance for the development of a larger health sector portfolio. This highly strategic role will include high-level relationship building, research project development and management, program and donor development, and developing a network of academic researchers. The successful candidate will have a strong track record in the development of health-focused research programs; comfort translating academic research into policy recommendations; strong networking capabilities with academic researchers, funders, and implementers; and the ability to represent IPA at high-level external policy and research events and meetings with key players in the health sector. Responsibilities Leadership and Quality Assurance of ARM’s Health Research Programs Set the technical direction for ARM's health research portfolio, including study design, measurement strategy, and standards for analysis. Oversee multi-country surveys and studies, including large-scale household surveys that collect biomarker data. Direct research that combines primary survey data with routinely collected health data, including health facility records, sentinel site reporting, and disease surveillance systems. Review and approve research designs, sampling strategies, power calculations, and pre-analysis plans across the portfolio. Serve as senior researcher on selected studies, including coverage surveys, program audits, and impact evaluations. Health Portfolio Strategy and Development Lead the development of a health sector vision and scope, including working closely with the Sector Programs Director and Deputy Director, the Senior Director of Business Development, the Chief Research and Policy Officer, and Country Directors to identify new health sector program opportunities Build and maintain relationships with donors, implementing organizations, government partners, and academic researchers. Work closely with IPA’s Business Development team to research potential health-focused funding opportunities, maintain a major donor list, and liaise with donors regarding funding opportunities and RFPs Write and edit grant proposals and supervise proposal development by others, including study design, budgets, and funder-facing narratives. Represent IPA's health research to academic and policy audiences through publications, presentations, and briefings. Team Leadership Hire, supervise, and develop a team of research scientists and research support staff. Mentor staff in survey methodology, evaluation design, and causal inference, and set standards for technical quality. Qualifications REQUIRED PhD or equivalent experience in public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, or a related field. At least 10 years of experience in applied health research, including experience leading research. Expertise in research methodology, including survey design, power analysis, sampling statistics, measurement of health outcomes, and evaluation design and causal inference. Experience with impact evaluation and post-event coverage surveys is required. Substantive expertise in one or more areas of public health. Demonstrated success in fundraising. Experience in proposal writing required. Ability to communicate clearly in writing and in person to both academic and policy audiences. Excellent English-language verbal and written communication, client management, and presentation skills. DESIRED Experience conducting research in Sub-Saharan Africa Expertise in infectious disease (malaria in particular), nutrition, water and sanitation, reproductive health, health delivery and systems, and/or vaccine delivery. Experience with large-scale household surveys that include biomarker collection. Experience working with routinely collected health data, including health facility records, sentinel site reporting, and disease surveillance systems. Qualitative research experience, or the ability to supervise qualitative researchers. Experience hiring, supervising, and developing research and program teams. Demonstrated project management skills, including budgeting, grant management and reporting, attention to operational and research details, and ability to manage multiple projects and/or proposals efficiently. A record of publication in public health, measurement, or survey research methods. Professional proficiency in French. Location IPA will consider candidates based in any country where IPA is registered (Nigeria, Ghana, Cote d’Ivoire, Sierra Leone, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Tanzania, Colombia, Peru, or the United States). The Principal Research Scientist and Director of Health Research will oversee research in several countries and will review data quality at the source, which requires occasional travel to program and data collection sites. Most of that travel over the next one to two years will be to Sub-Saharan Africa. Occasional travel for business development may also be required. Reports To Chief Research and Methods Officer (CRMO) Application Requirements To be considered for this role, applicants must upload a CV that lists their publications, including links (e.g., DOI, journal page, or working paper URL) where available. Applications that do not include a list of publications with links will not be reviewed. About IPA Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA) is a research and policy nonprofit that discovers and advances what works to improve the lives of people living in poverty. IPA brings together researchers and decision-makers to design, rigorously evaluate, and refine these solutions and their applications, ensuring that the evidence created is used to improve the lives of people living in poverty. In recent decades, trillions of dollars have been spent on programs designed to reduce global poverty, but clear evidence of which programs succeed is rare, and when evidence does exist, decision-makers often do not know about it. IPA exists to bring together leading researchers and these decision-makers to ensure that the evidence we create leads to a tangible impact on the world. Since our founding in 2002, IPA has worked with over 1,800 leading academics to conduct over 1,000 evaluations in over 60 countries. This research has informed hundreds of successful programs that now impact hundreds of millions of individuals worldwide. Safeguarding at IPA At Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA), we are committed to creating a safe and respectful environment for all individuals, particularly children and vulnerable adults. As IPA adheres to strict safeguarding principles, selected candidates will be expected to adhere to these standards. By joining IPA, you become part of a team dedicated to ethical conduct, social responsibility, and meaningful impact in the fight against global poverty. Together, we work to create a better world where everyone has the opportunity to thrive with dignity and respect.
